etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English possibilite, from Middle French possibilité (from Old French possibilite) and directly from Late Latin possibilitās (“possibility”), from Latin possibilis (“possible”); see possible. By surface analysis, possible +‎ -ity.

definitions.definition: A thing possible; that which may take place or come into being.

quote.citation: 2013 July 20, “The attack of the MOOCs”, in The Economist, volume 408, number 8845:
quote.text: Since the launch early last year of […] two Silicon Valley start-ups offering free education through MOOCs, massive open online courses, the ivory towers of academia have been shaken to their foundations. University brands built in some cases over centuries have been forced to contemplate the possibility that information technology will rapidly make their existing business model obsolete.

definitions.definition: An option or choice, usually used in context with future events.

quote.text: Mycelial lives are so other, their possibilities so strange.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) Capability, power or capacity to act.

quote.citation: 1593, anonymous author, The Life and Death of Iacke Straw […], Act IV:
quote.text: VVere Iacke Strawe a liue againe,And I in as good poſſibility as euer I was,I would lay a ſurer trumpe,Ere I would loſe ſo faire a tricke.
